summary.headline: SBI Card Q2 FY27 PAT rose 75% YoY to INR778 crore on lower credit costs, while spend growth was just 3% and NIM is guided range-bound around 10.8%.
summary.overview: SBI Card reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR5,141 crore (up 4% YoY) and PAT of INR778 crore (up 75% YoY), driven mainly by lower credit costs. Gross credit cost fell to 5.6% (down 98 bps QoQ and 342 bps YoY) and gross NPA to 1.9%. Total spends grew about 3% YoY to INR1,10,689 crore, with retail spends up 6% to a record INR95,299 crore, and management attributed the weak headline to festive timing shifting into Q3. Management expects receivables to grow from Q3 and retail spend growth of mid-teens to high-teens for FY27, but gave no receivables growth guidance. NIM was 10.8% with cost of funds up 18 bps QoQ to 6.8%, and management expects NIM to be range-bound as rate hikes feed in.

financial_highlights.metric: Daily weighted average cost of funds

segments.name: Retail spends
segments.commentary: Record INR95,299 crore in Q2, up 6% YoY; online was 62.8% of retail spend in H1 FY27. UPI spends on credit cards grew 17% QoQ, with INR21,300 crore of spends through UPI this quarter.

segments.name: Corporate spends
segments.commentary: INR15,390 crore in Q2, down QoQ; management says corporate is opportunistic, kept below 20% of total spend, and some spends were let go for margin reasons.

segments.name: Cards in force and acquisition
segments.commentary: Cards in force about 2 crore (32 lakh), up 8% YoY; more than 1 million new accounts added in Q2, up 18% YoY, with 49% from Banca and 51% from open market. Net addition of 8.6 lakh cards in FY27 to August.

guidance_outlook: Retail spend growth expected in the mid-teens to high-teens range for FY27 (management referenced a 14-16% range).
Receivables growth expected to start in H2 FY27 and from Q3; no numerical receivables growth guidance given.
NIM expected to be range-bound; cost of funds expected to rise over the next few quarters, with a possible further ~50 bps repo hike, impact expected to lag as the book reprices in about 60-75 days.
Gross credit cost expected around 6% for FY27 (management comfortable with 5.5%-6%), subject to geopolitical impact; management overlay of INR100 crore held.
Cost-to-income ratio guided at 57%-59% for FY27; no FY28 guidance given.
Quarterly run rate of more than 1 million new accounts to be maintained; Q3 opex expected to rise with festive spends.
capex_capacity: No capex plans, capital expenditure figures, or commissioning timelines were discussed on the call; the transcript contains no capacity or utilisation metrics for the business.
Operating cost was INR2,649 crore in Q2 FY27, up 7% YoY and flat QoQ; management attributed the flat run-rate to investment in business growth, with Q3 opex expected to rise on festive spends.

Cost-to-income ratio was 58.7% in Q2 (up 193 bps YoY); guidance for FY27 is 57%-59%. No FY28 cost-to-income guidance was given (management: 'Not as of now' for next year, aiming to reduce it if possible).
demand_pricing: Festive season started around 11 October 2026 versus 22 September 2025 last year, which management cites as the main reason for the weak YoY spend comparison.
EMI offtake is rising as mobile phone prices increase; point-of-sale EMI subvention moved from around 16% to 16.5-17% over recent months, and conversion-to-EMI rates were also raised.
Interchange income rose in Q2 as networks increased rates on certain categories; management says the higher level is sustainable within a range.
Revolver rate at 22% and interest-earning assets stable at 55%; EMI share of book at 33%, revolvers 22% of book, and 45% of portfolio is transactor.
Co-brand additions: Google Pay Flex SBI Card and Advantage SBI Card on YONO; Eternal co-brand card launched; existing co-brands include Tata Neu, PhonePe, Google Pay, Flipkart and BPCL.

qa_highlights.question: Will spends and receivables inflect in Q3, and how long will it take for spend growth to reach double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated that receivables growth starts in H2, from Q3. Spend growth is expected in the mid-teens to high-teens for FY27. Early festive EMI conversion trends are described as encouraging, but still early.

qa_highlights.name: How will NIM evolve given higher cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are optimising borrowing mix (working capital loans about 70-80 bps cheaper than CP), raising yields on the EMI book and converting transactors to EMI. Yield hikes are already in place, and management expects NIM to stay stable.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 6% credit cost guidance conservative given 5.5% run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY27 credit cost was 6.05%. Management sees 5.5%-6% as a comfortable range and does not expect credit costs to moderate much beyond that. The INR30 crore was a management overlay, not a provision.

qa_highlights.question: Why did corporate spends dip, and does opex stay in line?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate spends were let go for margin reasons. Opex was flat QoQ, but investment in growth was cited, and Q3 opex is expected to rise with festive spends. Cost-to-income guidance of 57%-59% is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the CIF bank share rise to 46%?
qa_highlights.answer: About 10% of the portfolio was reclassified after a granular review of account features and channels. Management said the previous quarter would have shown the same bank versus open-market split on the new basis.

risks_watch: Rate pressure: repo hike already done, with another ~50 bps expected; borrowing mix and EMI repricing must offset cost of funds to hold NIM at 10.8%.
Geopolitical and macro risk (West Asia conflict, energy prices, inflation) could raise credit costs; INR100 crore management overlay is held.
Receivables growth is still unguided; transactor share (45%) can move quickly and affect IEA and yield.
Opex and cost-to-income could drift up from Q3 with festive spending and customer acquisition.
Fee income and the regulatory focus on fee cuts across lenders; management says interchange grows with spends and instance-based fees with CIF.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and profitability, with strong emphasis on the credit cost trajectory. Cautious and somewhat evasive on receivables growth and FY28 NIM and cost guidance, repeatedly declining to quantify them ("early days", "not as of now").
key_quotes: And we stick to the guidance that we had given that the spends getting translated into receivables will happen in the second half and will start from Q3 itself.
So overall, yes, as you can see in our numbers also that around 18 basis points of cost has already increased.
So on the new customer acquisition, on the first wave of 4 years, 5 years back, when Amazon and Flipkart went with co-brand partners, we did not participate for profitability reasons

growth.why: Management guides FY27 retail spend growth of mid-teens to high-teens (14-16% referenced) and receivables growth from Q3, backed by co-brand launches, rising UPI and EMI offtake and a 1 million+ quarterly account run rate, but gives no numerical receivables guidance and no capacity additions; Q2 revenue rose 4% YoY while total spend grew only about 3%.
